extracted.intended_audience: administrative agencies, administrative law judges, agency counsel, and practitioners in administrative law
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory rules governing adjudications required by statute to be determined on the record after opportunity for an agency hearing (5 U.S.C. § 554). Covers applicability, required notice, opportunities to present evidence/arguments, decisionmaker duties and restrictions, and declaratory orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/Applicability of §554
rubrics_metrics.description: This section applies, according to the provisions thereof, in every case of adjudication required by statute to be determined on the record after opportunity for an agency hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicability is subject to the listed exceptions (see next item). It defines the class of proceedings to which the procedural protections in §554 attach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 554 does not apply to: (1) a matter subject to a subsequent trial of the law and the facts de novo in a court; (2) the selection or tenure of an employee (except an administrative law judge under section 3105); (3) proceedings in which decisions rest solely on inspections, tests, or elections; (4) the conduct of military or foreign affairs functions; (5) cases in which an agency is acting as an agent for a court; or (6) the certification of worker representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exceptions narrow the universe of adjudications covered by §554 and must be considered when determining whether §554 procedures apply to a given proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirements for persons entitled to a hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons entitled to notice of an agency hearing shall be timely informed of (1) the time, place, and nature of the hearing; (2) the legal authority and jurisdiction under which the hearing is to be held; and (3) the matters of fact and law asserted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When private persons are the moving parties, other parties must give prompt notice of issues controverted in fact or law; agencies may by rule require responsive pleading. When fixing time and place, agencies must give due regard to the convenience and necessity of parties or their representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to submit facts, arguments, and settlement proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall give all interested parties opportunity for (1) the submission and consideration of facts, arguments, offers of settlement, or proposals of adjustment when time, the nature of the proceeding, and the public interest permit; and (2) to the extent the parties are unable to determine a controversy by consent, hearing and decision on notice and in accordance with sections 556 and 557 of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires meaningful opportunity to present evidence and arguments and contemplates consideration of settlement where appropriate. Cross-references: sections 556 (hearings) and 557 (decisions and orders) provide additional procedural detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding employee must make recommended/initial decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The employee who presides at the reception of evidence pursuant to section 556 shall make the recommended decision or initial decision required by section 557, unless he becomes unavailable to the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presiding officer who hears the evidence is generally the one who prepares the recommended/initial decision, ensuring continuity between fact-finding and decisionmaking; unavailability is the limited exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on ex parte consultation about facts in issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Except to the extent required for the disposition of ex parte matters as authorized by law, the presiding employee may not consult a person or party on a fact in issue, unless on notice and opportunity for all parties to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures fairness by barring off-the-record fact consultations that could prejudice parties; permitted communications must be on notice with opportunity for participation by all parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on supervision/direction by investigative or prosecuting employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding employee may not be responsible to or subject to the supervision or direction of an employee or agent engaged in the performance of investigative or prosecuting functions for an agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains decisional independence of the factfinder from investigative/prosecutorial personnel to avoid conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bar on participation/advice by investigative or prosecuting employees in related decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee or agent engaged in investigative or prosecuting functions for an agency in a case may not, in that or a factually related case, participate or advise in the decision, recommended decision, or agency review pursuant to section 557, except as witness or counsel in public proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects against partisan influence by excluding investigative/prosecuting personnel from decisionmaking roles in the same or related matters; statutory exceptions: does not apply (A) in determining applications for initial licenses; (B) to proceedings involving the validity or application of rates, facilities, or practices of public utilities or carriers; or (C) to the agency or a member or members of the body comprising the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaratory orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency, with like effect as in the case of other orders, and in its sound discretion, may issue a declaratory order to terminate a controversy or remove uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives agencies optional authority to resolve disputes or clarify legal positions via declaratory orders; issuance is discretionary and has the same effect as other agency orders.
